text:
anya: kicking off onboarding intake for cedar13b-hybrid (13B, fp16 baseline, int8/int4 quant experiments). need a concise rollout + canary plan covering hosted, dedicated, and private. :rocket:

sam: +1. quick risk summary? any known quality deltas from evals?

anya: quick snapshot: int8 ~ parity with fp16 on most evals; int4 shows small degradation on dialog f1 (~1.6% drop) and a 0.8% drop on commonsense bench. latency p95 improvements: int8 -15%, int4 -35%. memory reduction int4 ~45%. full eval report: http://internal.ci/reports/cedar13b/summary

mai: can we get exact pass/fail thresholds? ops wants rollback criteria before any traffic shifts.

leon: propose thresholds:
- quality: any top-level eval metric drop >1.0% absolute (or >1.5% relative) => fail
- hallucination/spam metric doubles or increases by >1.5x => fail
- latency: p95 > 2x baseline or increase of >300ms => fail
- error rate (5xx) > 0.5% => fail
(agree?)

jordan: agree to those. add a monitoring probe: run eval set A (1000 prompts) every 1h during canary, diff and post to #eng-ml-evals. if dialog f1 drops >1% for 3 consecutive runs, auto rollback.

anya: good. rollout plan suggestion:
1) private (customer staging) canary: deploy int4 and int8 variants to customer-staging only, 0% public traffic. run 6h smoke + 24h evals.
2) dedicated pool canary: route 1% traffic to int8 variant only for 12h, if stable -> 5% for 24h.
3) hosted API: staged rollout int8 first (1% -> 5% -> 25%) over 48-72h, keep int4 as experimental behind flag.
4) fallback policy: if any fail criteria hit, immediate traffic shift to fp16/int8 baseline by automated policy.

sam: sounds safe. for dedicated/private we should also test kv-cache warmup patterns and prefix cache to ensure latency SLOs. add warmup script to smoke tests.

anya: warmup script is in the repo: `tools/warmup/cedar13b_warmup.py` — will run with `python tools/warmup/cedar13b_warmup.py --duration 10m --pattern mixed`.

leon: ops checklist items:
- ensure autoscaler min replicas >= 2 for canary pools
- enable detailed tracing (sample rate 100%) for canary window
- reserve burst capacity for Dedicated (20% headroom)

mai: quantization plan:
- A/B: int8 vs fp16 baseline for 48h internal traffic tests
- int4 only as gated experiment behind feature flag and explicit opt-in customers
- if int4 quality drop within tolerance, consider int4 for Dedicated-only tier (cost-optimized)

anya: sample canary traffic patch (for hosted)
```json
{
  "model": "cedar13b-int8",
  "traffic_allocation": {"cedar13b-fp16": 99, "cedar13b-int8": 1},
  "duration": "12h",
  "monitoring": ["eval-set-A-hourly", "p95-latency", "error-rate", "hallucination-rate"]
}
```

jordan: note: include synthetic adversarial prompts in eval-set-A to catch regression in safety / refusal behaviors.

leon: who owns the rollback automation? can we use an existing policy?

sam: deploy-bot has a rollout policy integration. tagging @deploy-bot will create a monitor and rollback hook. use policy `auto-fallback:v2` for this.

anya: action items:
- @mai run extended int8 vs fp16 internal 48h (metrics + evals)
- @jordan add adversarial prompts to eval-set-A and wire hourly runs
- @leon prepare dedicated pool autoscaler and tracing configs
- @sam wire deploy-bot `auto-fallback:v2` and confirm alerting channels (pager + slack)

deploy-bot: Canary manifest created for cedar13b-int8 -> started at 2160504421, canary id: cb-cedar-21605. Monitoring hooks attached.

anya: ETA for initial int8 internal run?

mai: starting now, will report first 6h snapshot in ~6h, full 48h run done in 48h. posting interim metrics to #eng-ml-evals.

sam: one more: cost note — int8 expected to reduce token cost ~22%, int4 ~40% if quality acceptable. include cost gating in final rollout decision.

anya: great. will reconvene after first snapshot. thanks all :thumbsup:
